spec.title: Context-Aware Task Execution with Smart Subagent Spawning
spec.context:
Large plans exhaust context before completion, requiring manual /clear calls between implementation waves. Task 029 (13 tasks, 630 lines) required several waves due to context exhaustion. Even with Claude Code's auto-compaction, task-specific details (line numbers, code snippets in action blocks) get lost during summarization.
Value: - Seamless execution of large plans without user intervention - Each task gets fresh subagent context with exactly what it needs - Main conversation stays lean for orchestration (~15% context) - No reliance on auto-compaction as a feature - Foundation for future parallel task execution

in-scope.item: Modify festina-implement to spawn subagents for task execution
Modify festina-plan to generate explicit context blocks per task
Add CLI commands for extracting individual task context from plans
Update plan.xml template schema with context element

out-of-scope.item: Parallel task execution (sequential only in this iteration)
Changes to task.xml or spec.xml formats
Complexity-based routing (simple inline vs complex subagent) - all tasks use subagents

requirements.requirement: festina-implement SHALL spawn a separate subagent (general-purpose type) for each plan task
Each subagent SHALL receive explicit file references to read, not embedded code snippets
Each subagent SHALL execute the task action, run verification, and report success/failure
The orchestrator SHALL persist task completion to plan.xml after each subagent finishes
The orchestrator SHALL stay under 30% context usage throughout execution
festina-plan SHALL generate context blocks for each task containing files to read
The context block SHALL include: existing files to read, pattern reference files, dependent file imports
CLI SHALL provide commands to extract individual task context from plan.xml
If subagent fails verification after fix attempts, orchestrator SHALL ask user how to proceed
Quality verification (TODO scan, requirement trace, wiring check) SHALL run in orchestrator after all tasks complete
Directive loading and compliance checking SHALL remain in the orchestrator (not delegated to subagents)

patterns.pattern: Task tool with subagent_type="Explore" for parallel agents. Spawn agents with prompts containing specific instructions and context.
Thin orchestrators route to handlers, ~100 lines. festina-implement becomes an orchestrator that delegates to subagents.
Tasks contain files, pattern, action, verify, done elements. Existing structure already has file refs; add context for explicit read list.

tasks/implement: Current execution is sequential, marks completion per task, code uncommitted

engineering.finding: patterns/orchestrator: Decompose large orchestrators, composition root wires components
patterns/subagent-orchestration: Stub doc to be completed after implementation

codebase.finding: festina-scope already uses Task tool with parallel subagents
festina-implement currently executes all tasks in main context
Plan.xml tasks have self-contained info but no explicit "read these files first" block

pitfalls.pitfall: Task complexity threshold: Decision - Always spawn subagent (every task gets fresh context)
Subagent prompt construction: Decision - Explicit file refs only (subagent reads fresh, lean prompts)
Subagents cannot spawn subagents: Standard mitigation - subagent must complete all work without delegation
Context estimation is approximate: Standard mitigation - orchestrator uses conservative buffer

constraints.constraint: Task tool subagent_type must be "general-purpose" for Edit/Write/Bash access
Subagents cannot spawn subagents (Claude Code limitation)
Sequential execution respects task dependencies (depends attribute)
Plan.xml must remain valid XML after context block addition
Directive loading and compliance checking stays in orchestrator (not passed to subagents)
